official.title: Doctoral Researcher in future ice conditions related risks on offshore wind and related energy systems
official.description_text:
At Aalto University, curiosity moves across disciplines, roles and communities. We bring people together to ask new questions, challenge familiar thinking and turn ideas into impact. Our work is rooted in responsibility, courage and collaboration, and in a shared commitment to shaping a more sustainable future.
The School of Engineering is inviting applications for a Doctoral Researcher in future ice conditions related risks on offshore wind and related energy systems
Research background and duties
At the Department of Energy and Mechanical Engineering, our Marine and Arctic Technology group develops numerical models of sea ice, such as discrete element simulations, to study ice loads on offshore structures and ship operations in ice. In this role, you will contribute to the ICROSS project, funded by the Det Norske Veritas Foundation, by studying how offshore wind farms and a changing climate alter sea ice conditions, such as ice deformation, ridging and fast ice. You will assess what these changes mean for ice loading and related risks to offshore wind infrastructure, such as damage to seabed cables from ridge keels, and for the safety of winter navigation in and near wind farms. Your results may also influence future design standards. The research is based on high-resolution numerical modelling of sea ice and may include coupling with large-scale sea ice models and analysis of observational data. The precise focus will be shaped together with your supervisor, the project team and stakeholders. Depending on the focus, your work may include:
Studying existing analyses, models and data on sea ice dynamics, ridging and ice–structure interaction
Further development of discrete element (DEM) simulations or continuum models for sea ice; DEM possibly coupled with large-scale sea ice models
Estimating how wind farms and climate change alter ice conditions and the resulting risks to offshore wind infrastructure
Providing ice condition results for assessing winter navigation risks induced by offshore wind farms
Contributing to the project's integrated cascading risk framework for offshore wind energy and shipping
Publishing in leading journals, presenting at conferences, joining stakeholder workshops and assisting in advising master's students
You will work closely with the ICROSS project team and with collaborators at CSC – IT Center for Science and the Finnish Meteorological Institute. Your doctoral research will be supervised by Associate Professor Arttu Polojärvi, and you will be part of the Marine and Arctic Technology research group. This is an exciting time to join us: offshore wind is expanding rapidly into ice-covered Nordic seas, and you will work with state-of-the-art sea ice simulation tools on questions that matter to industry and authorities.
What you bring
To thrive in this role, you will need:
A master's degree in mechanics, mechanical, civil or computational engineering, applied physics, oceanography, naval architecture or a related field
Solid coursework with excellent grades or research experience in above mentioned disciplines.
Prior experience with numerical modelling methods, such as the discrete element, finite difference or finite element method
Strong programming skills and motivation to work in a international and multidisciplinary team
We also value:
Demonstrated interest in sea ice physics and computational modelling of ice
Experience with C, C++, Python, MATLAB or similar programming languages
Experience in analysing observational data, scientific writing or academic publishing
Language requirements:
English: Good written and verbal communication skills in English are required.
We know that meaningful work is built by people with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. If you recognise yourself in the purpose of this role, we encourage you to apply and tell us what you would bring to our community.
What we offer
At Aalto, you can expect:
An internationally leading research environment in sea ice mechanics and ice engineering, within a large and active marine and arctic technology team.
Work with purpose in a community where research, education, creativity and services support meaningful change.
A multidisciplinary environment where collaboration, curiosity and new thinking are part of everyday work.
Extensive occupational health care services.
Staff-priced sport centre services on campus and at other UniSport locations.
A workplace on Aalto University’s Otaniemi campus, with excellent public transport connections and a wide range of services.
If you are chosen for this position, you will apply for the right to pursue doctoral studies at Aalto University School of Engineering. Doctoral studies at Aalto University typically take approximately 4 years. The position will be filled with a two-year contract, with the possibility of extension based on progress and performance. The planned starting date is February 2027. We support your professional growth with varied training and development opportunities shaped around your interests and aspirations.
Students in the final year of their master's programme are also welcome to apply, provided the degree is completed before the doctoral contract begins. Aalto University master's students may start working in the project by writing their master's thesis. The doctoral degree is awarded upon completion of doctoral coursework (30 ECTS), an article-based or monograph dissertation and a public defence.
The expected starting salary for a Doctoral Researcher is approximately 3,100 €/month (gross) and it increases as the Doctoral Researcher progresses in research and studies. Work-life balance and well-being in all aspects of life are essential for us at Aalto.
Curious to make a difference?
Please submit your application through our recruitment system
by December 15, 2026
. If you are already working at Aalto, please apply via our internal system Workday. If you are a student or visitor at Aalto University, please apply with your personal email address.  The position will be filled as soon as a suitable candidate is found, so we encourage you to apply early.
All applications must include the following materials:
Application cover letter / Motivation letter
with the applicant’s contact information and an indication of the preferred starting date (max 1 page)
CV
including details of all academic outputs
Contact information for two referees
Description of Master’s thesis project
(max 1 page)
Course transcripts of Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees with grades
(with a clear explanation of the grading scale).
All materials should be submitted in English in a single PDF file (compiled in the order specified above). Applications submitted by email will not be accepted. Aalto University reserves the right to leave the position open, extend the application period, and consider candidates who have not applied during the application period.
For more information about the role, please contact Prof Arttu Polojärvi (arttu.polojarvi(at)aalto.fi. For questions related to the application process, please contact hr-eng(at)aalto.fi.
About Aalto University
Aalto University builds on the legacy of three leading Finnish universities: Helsinki University of Technology, Helsinki School of Economics and the University of Art and Design Helsinki. Since 2010, we have brought science, art, technology and business together in new ways.
Today, the Aalto community consists of 16,000 students and 5,200 employees, including 446 professors. Half of our faculty members have an international background. Our campus in Espoo is a vibrant cluster of research and innovation with striking architecture, peaceful nature, open spaces for collaboration, and a wide range of services, all with excellent public transport connections. Diversity is part of who we are. We work actively to build a community where people can belong, contribute and grow.

ai.summary: Doctoral position in numerical modelling of sea ice dynamics and ice–structure interactions, using discrete element method (DEM) simulations to assess climate and offshore-wind impacts on Arctic ice conditions and infrastructure risks.

thematic_fit.rationale: This position is pure computational physics and marine engineering: sea ice mechanics, DEM modelling, ice–structure interaction, and climate hazard characterization. It has zero thematic connection to human-centred XR, immersive learning, spatial cognition, collaborative systems, or HCI methodology. The position is explicitly excluded from the researcher's target directions.

methodological_fit.rationale: The core methodology is high-resolution numerical modelling (DEM, continuum models, coupled simulations) and observational data analysis—a computational physics approach. The researcher's methodologies are experimental design, user studies, and XR application development. No methodological overlap. Programming skills (Python) are only a superficial match; the domain knowledge required is entirely foreign.

growth_value.rationale: Pursuing ice mechanics and DEM modelling would not advance the researcher toward human-centred immersive systems expertise. It represents a fundamental departure from the target trajectory and closes no capability gaps relevant to spatial cognition research, collaborative design, or HCI evaluation.

strategic_value.rationale: Aalto is priority-1 and Finland preferred; this institutional fit is valuable. However, the Marine and Arctic Technology group has no overlap with HCI-XR research communities. Supervisor (Arttu Polojärvi) specialises in ice mechanics, not human-centred systems. This group does not strengthen the researcher's network or credibility in target domains.

eligibility_flags: Researcher is MSc by Research (thesis stage); position accepts final-year candidates if degree completed before contract start (February 2027). Likely eligible but timing tight.

Position requires 'master's degree in mechanics, mechanical, civil or computational engineering, applied physics, oceanography, naval architecture or related field.' Researcher's MMU background in Multimedia/Creative Media does not meet stated disciplinary requirements.
risks: This position is explicitly listed in researcher's excluded_directions: 'pure-computer-vision, slam, robotics-control, graphics-rendering, gpu-optimisation, embedded-systems, pure-machine-learning-algorithms.' While not explicitly listed, pure computational physics (DEM, numerical modelling) aligns with the spirit of excluded pure-technical roles.
Major disciplinary mismatch (multimedia → sea ice physics); would signal career pivot unrelated to HCI trajectory.
Requires specialised computational physics knowledge (DEM, continuum mechanics, ice physics) with steep learning curve; researcher has no background.
4-year PhD commitment (with extension) in ice engineering delays entry to HCI-XR doctoral community and networks.
